clue.text: One out to spoil soccer knocked back drink in it

indicators.note: the drink is placed inside the word for soccer, the 'it' of the clue

parts.note: footer is an old public-school slang word for football

indicators.note: knocked back reads the drink backwards, as well as suggesting downing it

parts.note: beer is a common drink

explanation.surface: A football fan downs a drink in one while watching the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footer' is old British slang for football. 'knocked back' reverses the drink and also hints at downing it; 'in it' sets that inside the soccer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate or plunderer is someone whose aim is to spoil, in the old sense of taking plunder.

clue.text: Such as won't run quickly

definitions.meaning: ... colours or dyes do not run in the wash
... as an adverb means at speed

explanation.definitionFit: Dye that holds firm is described as colourfast, and rapid movement is also described this way.

clue.text: Love among heterosexuals

indicators.note: among tells us the answer lies inside the following word's letters

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love gives his name to erotic love generally.

clue.text: Expert letting society save pounds for a starter maybe

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

indicators.note: save in the sense of except tells us to leave out the pounds

parts.note: letting means allowing
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A financial expert lets a society keep its money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' here means except, so the pounds sign L drops out of the word for letting; 'starter' means an appetiser, and 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy chicken wings are often served as an appetiser, hence 'maybe' for an example.

clue.text: Rising chap failing to finish Open

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up
failing to finish removes the final letter of the name

parts.note: Trevor is a man's name, so a chap

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming golfer falls short of winning the Open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to finish' cuts TREVOR to TREVO, and 'Rising' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden.

clue.text: Provider of comfort I wondered about

indicators.note: about signals the letters being moved around

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who might offer them some comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet filled with soft duck feathers keeps a sleeper warm and comfortable.

clue.text: Only Eastern Scottish isle

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: The only island off Scotland's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off western Scotland.

clue.text: Revolutionary communist infiltrating uncovers secret

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: unwraps means uncovers

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A Marxist spy infiltrates and exposes a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' for a communist comes from the red flag; 'Revolutionary' turns it round and 'infiltrating' slips it inside the word for uncovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept under wraps is an idiom for hidden from view.

clue.text: Search in later rebuilt part of London

indicators.note: in places the search word inside the rebuilt letters
rebuilt means the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: scour means search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A hunt through a later redevelopment in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges the letters of later; 'in' then places the search word inside them, between EARL and T. Earls Court is an area of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court is a district of west London, known for its exhibition centre.

clue.text: Terrible wildness of bleak places

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess and need sorting

explanation.surface: The wilds have a terrible bleakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Expanses of permanent snow are desolate, inhospitable terrain.

clue.text: German or East European river

definitions.meaning: the river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland

explanation.definitionFit: The same word is German for the conjunction meaning alternatively and names a river on the Polish frontier.

clue.text: Spin doctor free with hot facts initially deniable

indicators.note: spin means to turn around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor hands out unattributed facts to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' rearranges DOCTOR FREE plus H and F ('facts initially').
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made unofficially can later be denied, as they were never on the record.

clue.text: Who's mixed in smartest fora?

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asks who is the type to mingle in the cleverest discussion groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges SMARTEST FORA; the whole clue also describes a graduate at home in learned forums.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a postgraduate degree might well move among clever debaters.

clue.text: Something to eat lacking money

parts.note: short means lacking, as in short of
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone without cash has nothing to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly Scottish biscuit made of butter, sugar and flour is a food.

clue.text: Thickset character of Spanish girl captured by artist

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: George Stubbs was an English painter famed for horses
Ines is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl is caught on canvas by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stubbs, the 18th-century English horse painter, is a frequent crossword artist; 'captured by' sets the Spanish girl's name inside his.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short and stocky is the quality of being squat and solidly built.

clue.text: One got into a stew by controversial subject

definitions.meaning: a potato is added to a hotpot, the Lancashire stew
an issue too awkward for anyone to handle

explanation.walkthrough: HOTPOT is a Lancashire stew of meat and potatoes, so a potato in it is read as 'hotpot a-to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue too sensitive to handle is compared to something too searing to hold.

clue.text: Lord let loose philosopher

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, such as a lord

indicators.note: let loose means set free, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A nobleman releases a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aristo' is informal for an aristocrat such as a lord; 'loose' rearranges the letters of let to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek thinker taught Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Trunk: extremity of elephant or such like

indicators.note: extremity points to the end letter of the word

parts.note: 'or so' means or such like, roughly

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk, or something of that sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The elephant's trunk is the obvious picture, but 'Trunk' is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the human body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Religious leader's endless talk

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, as in 'rabbit on'

explanation.surface: A clergyman's sermon goes on interminably.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit on' is British slang for talking at length; 'endless' drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish scholar and teacher leads a congregation.

clue.text: Look round in the vicinity of The Bull for him?

definitions.text: Look round in the vicinity of The Bull for him?

parts.words: Look round in the vicinity of The Bull for him?
parts.note: The Bull is a typical pub name, so the person in charge would be found around the pub

explanation.surface: Searching near a pub for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bull reads like an animal, but it is a pub name; the person sought runs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord or publican runs a pub such as The Bull.

clue.text: Woman in a rut could be deserting job

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else

explanation.surface: A woman stuck in a rut is thinking of quitting her job.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional singleton in Helen Fielding's diaries is a woman stuck in a rut of work and dating.

clue.text: What provides a measure of vision

definitions.meaning: a device fixed to an upturned bottle in a bar dispenses a measured shot
relating to the eyes and sight

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a bar spirit dispenser and describes things to do with sight.

clue.text: Protective covering for post

definitions.meaning: letters delivered by the postal service

explanation.definitionFit: The word names linked metal armour and also letters and parcels.

clue.text: It can make itself revert to type

definitions.text: It can make itself revert to type

parts.words: It can make itself revert to type
parts.note: a single wrong key can turn the word for a printing slip back into the word for printed letters

explanation.surface: Something that slips back into its old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revert to type' is the idiom for slipping back, but here one changed letter turns the word into TYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing error alters a word, and a single slip can change one word into another.

clue.text: Relations are finally over for them

definitions.text: Relations are finally over for them

parts.words: Relations are finally over for them
parts.note: people whose romantic relationship has ended

explanation.surface: Couples whose relationships have come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Former partners are people with whom a relationship has ended.

clue.text: Post needs fairly even characters still

parts.note: a station is a post, as in a duty station

indicators.note: even characters are the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A post office needs neat handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even characters' of FAIRLY are A, R, Y, added after STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless is not moving at all.

clue.text: Ruin a good looker

definitions.meaning: to ... someone's hopes is to wreck them

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to wreck hopes and is also slang for an attractive person.

clue.text: I called top to sort out minor offence

indicators.note: to sort out means to rearrange into order

parts.note: as printed this reads 'top'; the fodder must be I CALLED COP (cop being a police officer) to give two Cs and no T

explanation.surface: Someone summons a police officer over a petty crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sort out' rearranges I CALLED COP; the clue prints 'top', a slip, since the answer has two Cs and no T.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sin or trivial misdeed is a slight transgression.
